newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran urges extra security at Montevideo embassy.
newsitem.headline: Iran urges extra security at Montevideo embassy.

text.p: Iran has told Uruguay's ambassador it expected his country to provide additional security for its mission in Montevideo and arrest two armed men who attacked the embassy, the official news agency IRNA reported on Sunday.

It said the ambassador was summoned to the Foreign Ministry in Tehran on Saturday where he was told that Iran "expects the Uruguay government to provide additional security measures for protecting the Iranian embassy staff in Montevideo."
Iran would also "like to see the speedy arrest of the masked terrorists," the ambassador was told.

Iran's ambassador to Uruguay, Mohammad Ali Sarmadi, said on Friday two masked men armed with revolvers forced their way into Iran's embassy in Montevideo where they beat an official and threatened to detonate explosives before escaping.
"They wanted to kill me and then blow up the embassy," he told Reuters. "Nobody but the Zionists could do something like this, but the Uruguayan authorities will have to confirm that."

Uruguay is just across the River Plate from Argentina's capital Buenos Aires, which was the scene of bloody anti-Jewish bombings in 1992 and 1994. Israel and the United States blamed Iranian-backed guerrillas for the attacks, but Iran denied this.
